relations.subject: n1ql:set-transaction
relations.evidence: Currently, the only available transaction setting is `ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED`. This setting is enabled by default. The `SET TRANSACTION` statement is therefore optional and may be omitted.

notable_absence.finding: Like BEGIN TRANSACTION (already extracted this round), SET TRANSACTION carries no access-control gate at all - no Capella role requirement, no credential-type restriction, no named privilege. Its only prerequisite is behavioral/scoping ('You may only use this statement within a transaction'). This confirms across two pages in the transaction-statement family that the access-control model applying to DDL/DCL statements in this round simply does not extend to TCL statements - they inherit whatever gate applied to the enclosing transaction's first statement, and carry none of their own.

cross_component_finding: The page links out to server/'s transaction overview ('For an overview of Couchbase transactions, see [Transactions](../../../server/current/learn/data/transactions.md)') exactly as begin-transaction.md does, reinforcing that this whole TCL statement family is shared server/-authored conceptual content presented unchanged on the Capella docs tree.
cross_product_finding: Per the cross-round transaction check: no textual evidence on this page connects SQL++'s SET TRANSACTION (or the transaction it configures) to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction). The Related Links list only other SQL++ TCL statements, the server/ transaction overview, and a Couchbase blog post ('Couchbase Transactions: Elastic, Scalable, and Distributed'). No SDK cross-reference appears, so no relation is asserted - flagging as the same open question already raised against begin-transaction.json: whether SQL++ transactions and the Java SDK's distributed ACID transactions share an underlying mechanism remains unconfirmed by page text.
